## May 2027 TOK Essay Titles: Complete Student Guide


The **May 2027 TOK essay titles** are six prescribed questions for students taking the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme examination session in May 2027. You must choose **one title** and write a maximum of **1,600 words** , developing a clear, coherent, and critical exploration of the question.


The reported titles examine artistic and historical understanding, changing values, assumptions, coincidence, simplicity, and counterintuitive ideas. This guide explains what each prompt requires, which Areas of Knowledge may be useful, how to choose strategically, and how to plan a focused essay.


> **Important:** The six English formulations below have been widely reported, but the official IB title sheet is not currently available on a publicly accessible IB webpage. Confirm the exact wording and title number with your TOK teacher or school’s Programme Resource Centre materials. The official sheet supplied by your school is the final authority.


### The six reported May 2027 TOK essay titles


1.


**Do we gain a better appreciation of the human experience from the artist or the historian? Discuss with reference to the arts and history.**


2.


**If values change over time, how can they, nevertheless, continue to guide the pursuit of knowledge? Discuss with reference to two areas of knowledge.**


3.


**In the production of knowledge, how can knowledge be reliable if it is built on assumptions? Discuss with reference to the human sciences and one other area of knowledge.**


4.


**To what extent do you agree with the claim that “any coincidence is worth noticing; you can throw it away later if it is only a coincidence” (Agatha Christie). Answer with reference to mathematics and one other area of knowledge.**


5.


**In the production of knowledge, when choosing one explanation over another, to what extent should simplicity be prioritized? Discuss with reference to two areas of knowledge.**


6.


**In the pursuit of knowledge, what value is there in exploring the paradoxical or the counterintuitive? Discuss with reference to the natural sciences and one other area of knowledge.**


The wording of the prescribed title is part of the assessment task. Do not replace one with a general question about art, values, or science. The[official IB Theory of Knowledge page](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/dp-core/theory-of-knowledge/) provides general course context, while your official TOK materials explain the detailed requirements.


### What the TOK essay is assessed on


The TOK essay is an externally assessed component worth **67%** of the final TOK result. The exhibition contributes the remaining 33%. The essay is not a conventional literature essay or a test of how many facts you can include.


Examiners look for a **clear, coherent, and critical exploration of the prescribed title** . A strong response defines important terms in context, stays focused on the exact wording, develops claims and counterclaims, uses specific real-life situations, considers different perspectives, and reaches a qualified conclusion.


After introducing an example, explain what it reveals about evidence, assumptions, interpretation, reliability, perspective, or justification. A quotation or impressive case study cannot replace analysis.


### How to interpret each May 2027 title


### Title 1: **Do we gain a better appreciation of the human experience from the artist or the historian? Discuss with reference to the arts and history.**


This prompt asks you to compare two ways of understanding human life. **“Better appreciation”** might mean empathy, emotional insight, contextual understanding, or awareness of perspectives.


The arts can communicate the texture of experience through symbolism, imagination, form, and emotional involvement. A novel about displacement may develop empathy even though it is fictional, but its representation remains selective. History can provide evidence about events, institutions, causes, and groups, yet historians also interpret incomplete records through ideas such as significance and causation.


A strong thesis could distinguish emotional appreciation from contextual and evidential appreciation, rather than claiming that one AOK is always superior.


### Title 2: **If values change over time, how can they, nevertheless, continue to guide the pursuit of knowledge? Discuss with reference to two areas of knowledge.**


The word **“nevertheless”** creates the central tension: if values change across societies and periods, why should they guide knowledge production?


You could examine objectivity, transparency, human dignity, usefulness, justice, or intellectual freedom. In the human sciences, changing expectations about informed consent and privacy have influenced research practice. This may improve research conditions, but changing values can also create **presentism** , the uncritical imposition of current standards on the past.


A balanced argument might claim that changing values remain useful when they are explicit, open to criticism, and balanced against methodological standards.


### Title 3: **In the production of knowledge, how can knowledge be reliable if it is built on assumptions? Discuss with reference to the human sciences and one other area of knowledge.**


An **assumption** is not necessarily an unsupported guess. It may be a starting condition, simplification, theoretical commitment, or provisional belief that makes investigation possible.


In the human sciences, an economic model may assume rational behaviour, while a psychological study may depend on definitions of intelligence or wellbeing. These assumptions can support research but limit conclusions when they fail to represent the people or situations being studied.


Mathematics offers a useful contrast because systems rely on stated axioms and definitions. Conclusions can be reliable within the system when reasoning is valid, but mathematical consistency alone does not prove that a model accurately describes the empirical world. Evaluate whether assumptions are transparent, justified, appropriate, tested against evidence, and revised when necessary.


### Title 4: **To what extent do you agree with the claim that “any coincidence is worth noticing; you can throw it away later if it is only a coincidence” (Agatha Christie). Answer with reference to mathematics and one other area of knowledge.**


The quotation distinguishes **noticing a possible pattern** from accepting that pattern as meaningful knowledge. In mathematics, a numerical regularity may generate a conjecture, which must then be proved or disproved. A pattern in a small set of numbers is not evidence that it holds universally.


An unexpected correlation in the natural sciences may prompt valuable research, but it may also result from confounding variables, selection effects, or repeated testing. History can show how coincidences stimulate research and how people create misleading narratives retrospectively.


Pay attention to **“any.”** Noticing a coincidence can be useful, but investigating every coincidence may waste time and encourage confirmation bias. Distinguish between using coincidence as a prompt for inquiry and treating it as evidence.


### Title 5: **In the production of knowledge, when choosing one explanation over another, to what extent should simplicity be prioritized? Discuss with reference to two areas of knowledge.**


This title examines how knowers choose between explanations. **Simplicity** may mean fewer assumptions, fewer entities, or an economical model that explains many observations.


Occam’s razor does not mean that the simplest explanation is automatically true. In the natural sciences, simple models may be easier to test and communicate, but further evidence can require additional variables. In history, a single-cause explanation for a revolution may be memorable while ignoring interactions among political, economic, cultural, and individual factors.


Treat simplicity as a **heuristic** , or practical guide, rather than a substitute for evidence. Evaluate when it improves clarity and testability and when it becomes oversimplification.


### Title 6: **In the pursuit of knowledge, what value is there in exploring the paradoxical or the counterintuitive? Discuss with reference to the natural sciences and one other area of knowledge.**


**Counterintuitive** ideas conflict with ordinary expectations. A **paradox** may expose an apparent contradiction or a hidden problem in an argument. Neither term means automatically false.


Relativity challenged everyday assumptions about time, space, and simultaneity, while quantum theory produces results that are difficult to reconcile with ordinary intuition. These ideas are valuable because they can reveal that familiar ways of thinking are inadequate. Mathematics can also show how paradoxes expose hidden assumptions, while the human sciences may challenge stereotypes or reveal unexpected policy effects.


A surprising idea is not valuable merely because it is unusual. It must withstand critical testing, coherent reasoning, and comparison with other evidence.


### How to choose the best TOK title


Choose the prompt that supports the strongest sustained argument, not necessarily the one that sounds most interesting. Test each serious option by writing a provisional thesis, two claims, two counterclaims, and at least four specific real-life situations.


Test Question to ask yourself


Term clarity Can I define the central terms in context?


AOK fit Do the required AOKs create a meaningful contrast?


Examples Can I identify precise situations rather than broad topics?


Counterclaims Can I develop a genuinely plausible opposing view?


Evaluation Can I explain where my argument becomes weaker?


Conclusion Can I answer the exact qualification in the title?


The[guide to choosing a TOK essay title](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-choose-a-tok-essay-title-that-works-for-you) can help you identify a prompt’s central tension. The guide to[TOK essay titles and knowledge questions](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/tok-essay-titles-what-are-knowledge-questions) explains how to turn broad ideas into focused inquiry.


### A practical structure for a 1,600-word TOK essay


A useful planning framework is:


1.


**Introduction:** interpret the title, clarify key terms, identify the tension, and present a qualified thesis.


2.


**First AOK:** develop a claim, apply a specific example, analyse its significance, and test it with a counterclaim.


3.


**Second AOK:** show how the second AOK supports, qualifies, or challenges the first.


4.


**Comparison and evaluation:** connect the AOKs throughout, not only in the final paragraph.


5.


**Conclusion:** answer the title directly and state the limits of your judgement.


This is a framework, not a compulsory formula. The[TOK essay structure guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/tok-essay-structure) explains how to organize an argument without making every paragraph identical.


For each paragraph, ask: What knowledge claim am I making? What does my example reveal? What assumption or limitation complicates it? How does the paragraph answer the prescribed title?


Your three TOK essay interactions should show how your thinking developed. The Planning and Progress Form records planning and discussions with your teacher, but it does not replace the essay. Follow your school’s requirements for authentication, citations, and digital tools, and ensure the final work is your own.


### Common mistakes to avoid


-


**Changing the question:** Discussing a broad topic instead of the prescribed wording.


-


**Using vague examples:** Naming “social media” or “science” without a precise event, study, model, or controversy.


-


**Describing instead of analysing:** Retelling what happened without explaining its knowledge implications.


-


**Adding a token counterclaim:** Mentioning the opposing view without evaluating it.


-


**Comparing only in the conclusion:** Allowing the AOKs to remain separate throughout the essay.


-


**Relying on quotations:** Treating an authority’s words as a replacement for reasoning.


For planning and practice, use[RevisionDojo’s TOK resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/subjects/theory-of-knowledge) , including Study Notes, Flashcards, and question practice. After drafting,[TOK Essay Feedback](https://www.revisiondojo.com/tok-essay-feedback) can help identify problems with focus, examples, structure, and evaluation without replacing your authorship.


### Conclusion


The May 2027 TOK titles reward precise interpretation rather than broad discussion. Preserve the prescribed wording, use the required Areas of Knowledge purposefully, develop claims and counterclaims, and explain what each example reveals about knowledge.


Before choosing, test promising titles with a thesis, examples, and an opposing argument. Then revise every paragraph for relevance and analysis. RevisionDojo’s TOK Study Notes, Flashcards, Questionbank, Jojo AI, and TOK Essay Feedback can support this process, with feedback used to strengthen your own thinking and writing.
